chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu al-Maghra', from al-Halbi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) — similar to it.
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Al-Fudayl, and Zurara and Muhammad ibn Muslim, that they asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)
about buying meat from the markets, and it is not known what the butchers have done. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Eat, when that is in the markets of the Muslims, and do not ask about it.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to eat meat from the market if we don't know how it was slaughtered?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the principle of *istishab al-halaliyyah* (presumption of permissibility) for meat purchased in general Muslim markets, even if the specific slaughterer is unknown. It reflects the Shia juristic approach of relying on the general practice of Muslims rather than requiring strict verification of every detail, thereby facilitating daily commerce. This ruling is often contrasted with stricter views that require knowing the name of the slaughterer, highlighting the flexibility in Shia fiqh regarding market transactions.
